cards.explanation: Inserts, load jobs and streaming need no fine-grained read access on protected columns. UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE need Fine-Grained Reader, and INSERT SELECT needs it on the queried table.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The column-level-security intro says: 'If the write operation is an insert, fine-grained read access is not required'.

cards.statement: Looker stores a persistent derived table inside the Looker instance instead of in the connected database.
cards.explanation: Looker writes a persistent derived table into a scratch schema on the connected database and regenerates it on the schedule you set. The connection needs the Enable PDTs setting turned on.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The Looker derived tables page says a PDT 'is written into a scratch schema on your database'.

cards.statement: With a vector index in use, BigQuery VECTOR_SEARCH returns the exact nearest neighbors.
cards.explanation: VECTOR_SEARCH uses approximate nearest neighbor search when it uses a vector index. Searching fewer candidates trades recall for speed, so it can miss an exact nearest neighbor.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The vector-index page says that with an index the search uses ANN and 'recall might not be 100%'.

cards.statement: Cloud Marketplace orders decide whether a buyer keeps access to a Marketplace-integrated BigQuery sharing listing.
cards.explanation: Subscribing places a linked resource in the buyer's project, and an active Cloud Marketplace order keeps it accessible. Publishers can still add subscribers manually, outside Marketplace transactions.
cards.reason: Took the fact lens fix. The page also lets publishers 'manually add and update BigQuery sharing subscribers', and no order governs their access, so 'a subscriber' was arguable and 'a buyer' is not. The wording lens's keep does not conflict. Confirmed: 'Access to the linked resource is managed by active Cloud Marketplace orders' and 'Commercial subscriptions ... are managed by Cloud Marketplace orders'. I kept 'linked resource', as the page has it, instead of 'linked dataset'.

cards.statement: Data Studio connects a BigQuery data source with service account credentials from a key file the editor uploads.
cards.explanation: Editors enter only the service account's email. Admins grant the Data Studio Service Agent the Service Account Token Creator role on that account, so no key file is uploaded.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The Data Studio service account setup page says users need not download keys and upload them, and names the Token Creator grant to the service agent.

cards.statement: Managed Service for Apache Spark autoscaling adds workers when on-cluster HDFS utilization runs high.
cards.explanation: Autoscaling acts on YARN memory and, by default from image 2.2, YARN cores. Google says it is not intended for scaling on-cluster HDFS, because HDFS utilization is not an autoscaling signal.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The autoscaling page covers the image 2.2 YARN cores default and says HDFS utilization is not a signal.

cards.statement: A folder's reservation assignment overrides the assignment of a project inside that folder in BigQuery.
cards.explanation: A project uses its single most specific reservation assignment. A project assignment overrides a folder assignment, which overrides an organization assignment.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The reservations page says 'a project assignment overrides a folder assignment'.

cards.statement: BigQuery adds a job's labels to billing data, so a Cloud Billing export can group on-demand query charges by job label.
cards.explanation: Job labels reach billing data. Dataset labels appear only in storage billing data and table or view labels not at all, so teams label jobs to attribute query costs by team or workload.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The adding-labels page says job labels are included in billing data. Statement 119 characters.

cards.statement: Dataset owners query BigQuery fail-safe data themselves once a table's time travel window has ended.
cards.explanation: Fail-safe storage retains deleted data for emergency recovery, but users cannot query or recover it directly. Recovering data from fail-safe goes through Cloud Customer Care.
cards.reason: Both lenses keep. The time-travel page says: 'You can't query or directly recover data in fail-safe storage'.
